text:
The gain is the failing spec. The simulated a1 = -0.0266 matches the ideal inverting gain -Rf/R1 = -1059.2/37903 = -0.0279, so the op-amp is working and the feedback ratio is wrong. The target midpoint of about -1.3e-3 is roughly 20× smaller in magnitude, which points to R1 being about 21× too small (roughly 0.8 MΩ, consistent with the 1 MΩ values used elsewhere in the netlist). Rf at 1 kΩ is already a sensible value, so a fault there would require an implausible ~50 Ω. The large sensitivity of a1 to R1 and Rf confirms the gain is set by these two resistors alone. The MOSFETs barely affect a1, and the bandwidth, power and offset specs all pass.

This makes the inverting gain -Rf/R1 about -0.028 V/V (simulated -0.0266) instead of the required about -1.3e-3 V/V. Restoring R1 to roughly 796 kOhm should bring a1 into the [-1.56e-3, -1.04e-3] window."}
